plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: Bare, gnarled branches break into fragrant blossoms in white, blush and deep rose, often while frost is still in the air. Each flower is about the size of a thumbnail. The scent is spicy-sweet and carries well on cold air. Japan's famous plum groves are a favorite place to see them.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring, roughly February to March, with the flowers opening before the leaves
plants.location: Japan, including its famous plum groves and festivals, and across East Asia
plants.funFact: Ume blooms weeks before cherry blossoms, so in East Asian culture it is a symbol of perseverance and the first promise of spring. Its green fruits are pickled as umeboshi and steeped in liqueur.

plants.name: Galanthus nivalis
plants.description: Nodding, white, bell-shaped flowers hang from slender stems above grey-green strap leaves. Each bloom has a small green mark on its inner petals. Snowdrops carpet woodland floors and churchyards in drifts, often pushing up through frost or snow.
plants.bloomingSeason: Typically January to February, and increasingly earlier in mild winters
plants.location: Woodlands, gardens and churchyards across the United Kingdom and much of Europe
plants.funFact: Snowdrops make a natural antifreeze-like protein that helps them cope with cold. Their bulbs are also the original source of galantamine, a compound used in medicine.
